title: Request for Deeper Overhead Stowage Compartments in the Forward Cabin
abstract: Operator asks for deeper forward-cabin overhead bins to reduce gate-checked bags; declined because the required bin depth cannot be certified against head strike criteria without a cabin re-layout the operator will not accept.

sections.request: We gate-check bags on nearly every departure out of our main base and it costs us time we do not have on a thirty minute turnaround. Our cabin crew tell us the forward bins fill first because that is where the business cabin boards, and once they are full the rest of the cabin starts handing bags over at the door. We would like the forward bins made deeper so that a standard roller bag goes in wheels-first rather than flat. We understand this may mean the bin sits slightly lower. We are willing to accept that if it lets us board without gate-checking. We would want it on the aircraft we already have, not just on new deliveries.
sections.background: We have measured the problem over a full season: on average nine gate-checked bags per departure from our base, and a two to three minute delay on about a fifth of departures where the last bags have to be taken forward. We looked at a cabin re-layout to move the business cabin aft but rejected it because of the impact on our product. Two other operators of the type have asked us informally whether we were pursuing this.
sections.expected_outcome: Deeper forward overhead bins retrofittable during a scheduled layover, keeping the existing seat pitch and the existing cabin layout, and with no reduction in certified passenger capacity.

type_data.business_justification: Nine gate-checked bags per departure and delay exposure on roughly one departure in five at the operator's main base; the commercial case was accepted but the technical case was not.
type_data.closure_note: Rejected on 30 March 2026. The bin depth the operator asks for cannot be achieved without lowering the bin base below the head strike envelope certified for the current seat pitch, and the only compliant answer is a cabin re-layout that moves the business cabin aft. The operator has stated that it will not accept that re-layout, so no technically compliant solution exists inside the constraints given. The commercial case was accepted and the request has been passed to the cabin product roadmap for consideration on a future seat product rather than as a retrofit.
